# MAC mask can lose leading digits when typing after refocus

Promoted from Julia’s observed component-test failure after a second occurrence on a stylesheet-only PR. Maintainer lane for the Engine 14 cut because the same failure holds two unrelated PR checks.

## Context
`test/playwright/component/form/field/PrefixField.spec.mjs` acquired a full Input masks workbench case in [PR 21774](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21774). Its mixed-case MAC scenario failed after refocus on two heads:

- [Drag cancellation e8ad080d49](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44916491157/job/136883584310) received `01:a2:B3:c4:D5:eX`.
- [ThemeSwitcher CSS 0957bf2fd8](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44911682433/job/136868921271) received `1a:2B:3c:4D:5e:XX`.
- [Exact-head drag retry, attempt 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44916491157/job/136888651673) reproduced `1a:2B:3c:4D:5e:XX` at line 181. The other 245 component cases passed. The uploaded result has the assertion and DOM snapshot. The next failing run needs an input/caret trace.
- [Dev 2c0ac855f9](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44911332316/job/136867735045) passed the same test on the corresponding shard.

## The Problem
Open the Input masks workbench and run the sequence in [the component spec](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/22f31c47a422fbbb26c485cfea051ce9945ca965/test/playwright/component/form/field/PrefixField.spec.mjs#L170-L181): clear the MAC field, type rejected letters, blur, verify the empty field, refocus and immediately type `GG00ZZ1a2B3c4D5e` with zero delay. The expected stored/displayed sequence is `00:1a:2B:3c:4D:5e`. The CI failures lose leading accepted digits.

## The Architectural Reality
Design authority comes from the workbench acceptance in `#21502` and the zero-delay ordering check in `#21555`. [The Main addon](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/22f31c47a422fbbb26c485cfea051ce9945ca965/src/main/addon/PrefixField.mjs#L115-L179) formats on focus and input synchronously and forwards synthetic input to the App Worker. The spec waits for addon registration before testing. A focus-mask readiness gap and a later value/caret write are hypotheses. The CI logs establish the missing digits and leave the mechanism open.

## The Fix
Replay the failing sequence on current `dev`. Capture value, caret and input events from blur through the first two accepted zeroes to identify the failing boundary. Keep the repair in the existing fixture if the test starts before its intended input state, or repair the owning input path if a user can lose digits after a normal focus. Use the existing component spec to prove the selected fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The mixed-case refocus sequence preserves both leading zeroes, strips rejected letters and retains separator placement. Keep zero delay between keystrokes.
- [ ] Repeated headless runs of the workbench test preserve the uppercase, lowercase, empty blur and Reset assertions. Record the repeat count and the evidence locating the failure or readiness boundary.

## Out of Scope
ThemeSwitcher styles, drag cancellation, changes to the MAC grammar and blanket sleeps or retries in the test.

## Current `dev` headless evidence
At `22f31c47a4`, the existing Chromium workbench case passed the MAC mixed-input assertion in **16/16** repeats. An isolated four-page probe replayed the MAC sequence **32/32** times and saw no late empty-value Main delta after refocus. The CI failures above remain the positive evidence for the MAC symptom.

The existing case failed **12/16** times at the later phone assertion (line 206), with `+1 (___) ___-____` in place of `+1 (555) 234-5678`. At the first empty-field observation after Reset, a separate trace saw the restored placeholder while the Main addon still used pattern `AB-___` and filter `[A-H]` (16/16 observations). In that probe, immediate input passed **6/8** and input after the addon reported both restored configs passed **8/8**. This records a Reset readiness gap in the same test, with its own evidence.

### Causal control on `dev` (`22f31c47a4`)
A headless observer recorded an actual empty-value write from `DeltaUpdates.updateNode` after blur. The timing arm held only that redundant write, preserving the addon’s synchronous clear, and applied the real write after the selected trusted input event. It injected neither a new delta nor synthetic typing.

| Arm | Result | Repeats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native timing control | `00:1a:2B:3c:4D:5e` | 5/5 |
| Actual clear applied after first zero | `01:a2:B3:c4:D5:eX` (CI attempt 1) | 5/5 |
| Actual clear applied after second zero | `1a:2B:3c:4D:5e:XX` (CI attempt 2 and the CSS-only PR) | 5/5 |

Just before the delayed write the DOM held `0X:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX` or `00:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX`. The write set the value to `''` and reset selection to `0..0`. This establishes a production write that can cause both reported failures under delayed delivery. The hosted failure artifacts do not record the write order.

Next: use the existing held-render test in `InputValueSync.spec.mjs` to distinguish a redundant native clear echo from a deliberate programmatic clear. Retain the model’s null empty value while keeping the native empty string in VDOM if the test confirms where the redundant delta originates.

### Source-Traced Mechanism (`PrefixField.mjs:161-179` → `Text.mjs:557` → `DeltaUpdates.mjs:909-911`)

Traced the exact cross-worker clobber path so you don't need an extra CI runner trace run, @neo-gpt-sophie:

1. **Blur (`PrefixField.spec.mjs:175` → `src/main/addon/PrefixField.mjs:174-179`):**
   `onFocusOut` sets `el.value = ''` **synchronously** on Main and calls `this.dispatchSyncInput(state)`, queueing an App → VDom → Main update (`Text#afterSetInputValue` at `src/form/field/Text.mjs:557` → `{attributes: {value: ''}}`).
2. **Immediate refocus (`PrefixField.spec.mjs:176-179` → `PrefixField.mjs:161-163`):**
   Because `await expect(macInput).toHaveValue('')` on `:176` reads Main's synchronous `el.value = ''` at `0ms`, Playwright immediately runs `await macInput.click()`, where `onFocusIn` sets `el.value = 'XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX'` (`selection: 0..0`) and calls `this.dispatchSyncInput(state)` again — queueing a second App → VDom → Main update (`{attributes: {value: 'XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX'}}`).
3. **Why M5 Max passes `32/32` while 2-vCPU CI loses `'0'` or `'00'` (`src/main/DeltaUpdates.mjs:909-911`):**
   On local M5 Max (`< 1ms` worker IPC), both `dispatchSyncInput` VDOM echoes settle inside `await macInput.click()` (`mousedown` → `mouseup`) before `pressSequentially('GG00ZZ1a2B3c4D5e', {delay: 0})` begins. Under 4-worker CI load (`10–30ms` worker roundtrip), `pressSequentially` has already written `'0'` (`"0X:XX:..."`) or `'00'` (`"00:XX:..."`) into `el.value` on Main when the in-flight `onFocusIn` VDOM `updateNode` delta arrives at `DeltaUpdates.mjs:909-911` (`if (key === 'value') { node[key] = val }`), overwriting the active `<input>.value` back to `'XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX'` (and resetting caret selection) right before `'1a2B3c4D5e'` types into slots `0..9` — yielding exact observed strings `"01:a2:B3:c4:D5:eX"` (1 digit before echo) and `"1a:2B:3c:4D:5e:XX"` (2 digits before echo).

*(Same echoed-`value` mechanism explains a fast human typist losing their first digit after focusing an empty masked field on a busy tab — guarding echoed untouched-mask `value` writes on an actively edited `PrefixField` input, or suppressing `notifyWorker` for untouched-slot mask display on `focusin`/`focusout` if App Worker `Text.value` shouldn't store literal `'XX:XX:...'` placeholders, fixes the engine path directly.)*
